Wipe
wīp
v. (to rub clean or dry; rendering Hebrew machah, Greek exaleipho)
Old English wipian. Scripture's wiping runs from a dish scoured out in judgment to tears removed by God's own hand.

Biblical Definition

To wipe is to rub clean. God's judgment on Jerusalem uses a domestic image: “I will wipe Jerusalem as a man wipeth a dish, wiping it, and turning it upside down” (2Ki 21:13). The promise reverses it: “he will swallow up death in victory; and the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces” (Isa 25:8), repeated twice in Revelation — “God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes” (Rev 7:17; 21:4).

Webster 1828 Definition

Webster (1828) defines wipe as to rub with something soft for cleaning; to clean by rubbing; and to strike off gently, to efface, to obliterate.

expand to see more

WIPE, v.t. To rub with something soft for cleaning; to clean by rubbing; as, to wipe the hands or face with a towel.

2. To strike off gently.

3. To efface; to obliterate; to remove.

4. To cheat; to defraud.

Key Scripture

2Ki 21:13 — "And I will stretch over Jerusalem the line of Samaria, and the plummet of the house of Ahab: and I will wipe Jerusalem as a man wipeth a dish, wiping it, and turning it upside down."

Isa 25:8 — "He will swallow up death in victory; and the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces; and the rebuke of his people shall he take away from off all the earth: for the LORD hath spoken it."

Rev 7:17 — "For the Lamb which is in the midst of the throne shall feed them, and shall lead them unto living fountains of waters: and God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes."

Rev 21:4 — "And God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes; and there shall be no more death, neither sorrow, nor crying, neither shall there be any more pain: for the former things are passed away."

Modern Corruption

Heaven is described as a place without sorrow, and Scripture describes something more personal — God's own hand removing tears from particular faces.

expand to see more

Revelation 21:4 is worded with unusual intimacy: God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes. Not the tears will cease, not sorrow will be forgotten — a hand goes to a face. The verse assumes there are tears there to be wiped, which means the grief carried into that moment is not denied or minimized on arrival. It is attended to, personally, by God.

2 Kings 21:13 uses the same verb for the opposite work: I will wipe Jerusalem as a man wipeth a dish, wiping it, and turning it upside down. The picture is thorough and domestic — a dish scoured out and inverted so nothing remains in it. Set beside Revelation, the two uses show the range of the same hand: what it does to a city under judgment, and what it does to a face in glory.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

Hebrew machah (H4229), to wipe, blot out; Greek exaleipho (G1813), to wipe away, obliterate — also used of blotting out sins.

expand to see more

Hebrew machah (H4229) — to wipe, blot out; 2 Kings 21:13, Isaiah 25:8, Genesis 6:7.

Greek exaleipho (G1813) — to wipe away, blot out; Revelation 7:17, 21:4, Acts 3:19, Colossians 2:14.

Greek dakruon (G1144) — tear; the object of the wiping.

Usage

"“As a man wipeth a dish… turning it upside down” — judgment made domestic."

"“The Lord GOD will wipe away tears from off all faces” — Isaiah's promise."

"“God shall wipe away all tears from their eyes” — a hand to a face."
